entries.summary: Leave hours count toward the week totals, so they match Rotageek
entries.details:
Team Calendar (week view)
- Your booked leave now counts in your Hours figure, like it does in
  Rotageek and on the Shifts page. 2–8 Nov reads 22h 45m (+2h 45m over)
  instead of 10h 45m (-9.3h under); 23–29 Nov reads 22h 30m (+2h 30m over)
  instead of 18h 30m (-1.5h under).
- Each Annual Leave chip shows the hours it's worth (4h a weekday on a 20h
  contract; weekend days inside a leave range carry none, as in Rotageek).
- Over / under is shown in exact hours and minutes, so 9h 15m no longer
  reads as "9.3h".
- Colleagues' leave still adds nothing: it's entered without hours.

Calendar (month view)
- Each week's figure on the right is now one total, shifts + leave, and
  it matches Rotageek's Total column: 20 / 22.75 / 23.5 / 20 / 22.5 /
  23.75 for November 2026. The leave chip underneath shows how much of it
  is leave; a "done so far" chip appears while a week is part-worked.
- The first week of the month gets its total even when the leave or
  shifts in it fall in the previous month (26 Oct – 1 Nov showed nothing
  for 20h of leave).
- Shift cells, Hours Worked and the week totals all use paid hours
  (scheduled break taken off), which is what pay is worked out on. The
  09:45–15:45 shift showed 6.00h next to £77.51 — that's 5.75h of pay.
- New Annual Leave stat square with the month's leave hours.

entries.summary: Phone layout pass: stats, both calendars, settings and date boxes
entries.details:
Stat squares
- On a phone the stat squares are all on screen, three across, instead of
  a strip you had to scroll sideways to see the rest of. The Shifts page's
  "Breaks & distance" fold works on phones too.

Calendar
- Under the month grid there is now a list of the month's shifts with the
  time, hours, pay, early/day/late tag and any note. It starts at today,
  with earlier shifts one tap away. Tap a row to edit that shift.
- Add Shift is a floating button above the tab bar on Shifts and Calendar,
  and the month and year pickers get the whole row.

Team Calendar
- The toolbar is one tidy row: previous / next week, Today, Add Shift.
  The year and month jumps, refresh, export and bulk deletes are behind
  "More".
- On a phone each person is one line (name, hours, time, edit, delete)
  rather than wrapping onto two or three, and a row of day chips at the
  top jumps straight to a day. A dot on a chip marks a coverage gap.
- On a computer the small edit / delete buttons no longer sit on top of
  the shift's end time; they appear when you hover the cell.

Settings and forms
- Settings: "+ Add Schedule" and "+ Add Rate" no longer cover the section
  title on a phone. They show once the section is opened.
- Date boxes: the calendar icon is inside the box at its right-hand end,
  so it can no longer drop onto its own line underneath. Tap it to pick a
  date.
- Radio buttons and tick boxes that had ballooned into large blobs (for
  example Export's date range) are normal size; Export's date-range
  choices are tappable chips.
- The grey "secondary" buttons (Copy, Generate token, Prev / Next and
  others) were unstyled and showed as bright white in dark mode.

entries.summary: Trimmed to the useful features, with one Features page
entries.details:
Removed
- The novelty pages: Trophy Cabinet, Record Book, Shift DNA, Work-Life
  Balance, On This Day, Rota Bingo, Countdown Board, Shift Briefing, Head
  to Head, Did You Know (fun facts) and Rota Crystal Ball.
- From the older extras: Synergy Score, Shift Heatmap, Streaks & Badges
  and Rota Wrapped.
- The app-watching-itself analytics: App Usage, Screen Time and Check
  Habits.
- Nothing you entered is deleted. The database tables behind these pages
  are left in place, and an old link or bookmark to a removed page opens
  the Features page instead.

Kept
- Every base page (shifts, calendar, clocking, payslips, leave, reports,
  insights, team, import/export, settings and so on).
- Money Clock, Pay Forecast, Pay Audit, Tax Check, Overtime Tracker, Pay
  Rise History, What If?, Goal Tracker, Savings & Share Plans, Commute
  Cost, Break Debt, Annoying Shifts, Year in Numbers, Leave Optimiser,
  Cover Finder, Weather, Team Metrics, Fatigue Audit, Data Doctor, Clock
  Map and Data & Privacy.

One Features page
- The three separate hubs (V2.0, V3.0, V5.0) are now a single Features
  page, grouped into Money, Rota, Team and Upkeep, with one "Features"
  row in the menu in place of the "More" group.

Lighter
- The app no longer logs every page you open. Visits are only recorded
  alongside GPS fixes, while location tracking is switched on for the
  Clock Map. With location off (the default) nothing is recorded.
- 20 fewer pages: the second code bundle is about 12% smaller.

entries.summary: Shorter menu, folded-away stats, readable status colours, shortcuts
entries.details:
Menu
- The sidebar is down to the four pages used every day (Dashboard, Shifts,
  Calendar, Clock In/Out) and four groups: Pay & Leave, Team, More and
  Tools. Only one group is open at a time.
- Settings, dark mode, Hide Money and Edit menu are now a row of four icon
  buttons at the bottom instead of four full-width rows.
- The three feature hubs sit together under More as Features, Extras and
  Analytics. Weather moved into Extras.
- Menu icons are greyed back until hovered or selected, so the labels and
  the current page stand out.
- On a phone the burger button in the top bar is gone; the tab bar's Menu
  button (or a swipe from the left edge) opens the menu.
- If you have saved your own menu layout it is kept as it is. Use the
  pencil button, then Reset, to switch to the new layout.

Shifts
- The six headline numbers stay at the top; the break and distance figures
  fold away behind "Breaks & distance", so the shifts themselves are on the
  first screen. The choice is remembered.

Colours
- Green, amber, red and blue used as text on white (pay figures, plus and
  minus differences, break chips, badges) were too pale to read easily.
  They are a step darker in light mode. Dark mode is unchanged.

Shortcuts
- Left and right arrows step the month on Shifts and Calendar, the week on
  Team Calendar and the leave year on Leave. T goes to today, N adds a
  shift. On a phone, swipe the Calendar left or right to change month.
- The Key page lists all the shortcuts.

entries.summary: New indigo look, colour-coded shifts, phone tab bar and quick search
entries.details:
Look
- The yellow theme is replaced with indigo throughout (light and dark), with
  a darker sidebar and a tidier logo. Every yellow tint now comes from one
  set of colour settings, so the accent can be changed in one place.
- With no saved choice, dark mode follows your phone or computer setting.

Shifts
- Shifts are colour-coded by when they start: amber for early (before
  09:00), blue for day (09:00 to 11:59) and violet for late (12:00 on).
  Shown on the Calendar, the Shifts list and the Dashboard's Coming Up, and
  explained on the Key page.

Getting around
- Phone: a tab bar along the bottom for Home, Shifts, Calendar, Clock and
  the full menu.
- Quick search: the search button in the top bar (or Ctrl/Cmd+K, or "/")
  finds any page by name, including the ones inside the V2/V3/V5 hubs, and
  remembers the ones you opened last. It can also add a shift or switch
  dark mode and Hide Money.
- Esc closes a dialog or the phone menu; the page behind a dialog no longer
  scrolls; opening a different page starts at the top; the browser tab
  shows the page name.

Speed
- The six stylesheets are served as one file, so the page needs one request
  instead of six before it can draw.

Fixes
- The calendar button on full-width date boxes sat on its own line under
  the box; it now sits inside it.
- "Edit menu" in the sidebar was dark text on a dark background.
- The browser smoke test never noticed the minified bundle was ready, so it
  was testing the unminified one.

entries.summary: Dark mode — fix unreadable text (leaderboard, tabs, links, icon buttons, chips)
Insights — break untaken time and pay as stats at the top
Midnight sync shown as a small always-on status pill instead of a banner
Automatic midnight sync — silent, audited, with a dashboard banner
Payslip upload — drop the Month box unless a file name has no month
Read Paystub_YYYYPP names as tax year + tax month (verified against all 21 PDFs)
Grey out the payslip upload Month box when every file name already says its month
Bulk payslip upload — month read from file name (Paystub_YYYYMM.pdf), renamed to Month - Year, with a preview
Payslip documents auto-name to Month - Year, and can be uploaded from the payslip popup
Annoying Shifts works for colleagues too
Annoying Shifts page counting short, midday, evening, split and quick-turnaround shifts
Limit full-history sync/compare to start from 12 May 2026
More varied fun facts, and Gemini model "Auto" in Settings
entries.details:
Fun facts
- The deck has a lot more to say: weekends and bank holidays worked, your
  earliest start and latest finish, longest run without a day off, breaks
  skipped, tax and National Insurance paid, leave taken, average pay per
  hour, how many colleagues you've worked with, your biggest week, how long
  ago your first shift was, and your earliest clock-in.
- The AI bonus fact now picks a different topic each time (time, pay, tax,
  weekends, early/late shifts, colleagues, breaks, leave or commute) and only
  sees that topic's numbers, so it stops turning everything into miles.
  "Get another" never repeats the topic it just showed.

Settings → AI Screenshot Import
- New "Auto" model choice (and the default): uses the newest everyday model
  your key can use and switches itself if one runs out of free allowance.
- The model list now labels the best all-rounder, the fastest and the most
  accurate, with a short note on which to pick. Text-to-speech and
  image-generation models are no longer listed.
- Your saved model isn't changed — pick Auto in Settings to switch.

entries.summary: Miles driven now agree everywhere (round trip)
entries.details:
Stats
- Trophies (Road Warrior), the Records page ("Miles driven" and marathons),
  Wrapped ("driven to work this year") and Year in Numbers were showing the
  ONE-WAY distance, half of what the "You have driven N miles to work" card
  and the Commute Cost page show. They now count there and back, so the
  numbers match. Your Road Warrior progress will go up accordingly.
- Importing shifts with both a "miles there" and a "miles back" column used
  to add the two together, which got doubled again in every total. It now
  stores their average as the one-way distance.
- The shift form and Settings now say the distance is one way.

entries.summary: Fun fact miles now match the "driven to work" card
entries.details:
Fun fact
- The AI bonus fact and the "You have driven N miles to work" card showed
  different totals (2,520 vs 5,040). The card counts the round trip; the AI
  fact was only being given the one-way distance, so it showed half. Both
  now use the round trip.

entries.summary: Fun facts try another Gemini model when one is out of quota
entries.details:
Fun fact
- When the Gemini model you've chosen has used up its free quota, the fun
  fact now tries another model instead of showing Google's long error. It
  remembers which model is used up for a while, so the next fact doesn't
  wait on it again.
- If every model is out of quota, the message is now a plain "Gemini's free
  quota is used up ... try again later".

entries.summary: AI rename and screenshot import skip models that can't see images
entries.details:
Photo Library / Team Upload
- If the AI model chosen in Settings can't read images (the "Image input
  modality is not enabled for this model" error), the app now moves on to
  another model that can, instead of failing every photo. It remembers
  which model that was, so running the rename on all your past photos
  doesn't waste a try on it each time.
- Text-only models (audio, text-to-speech, image-generation and the like)
  are no longer offered in the model list in Settings.
- If no model can read the image, the error now says so and points to
  Settings → AI Screenshot Import.

entries.summary: Removed "Best Days to Book Leave" from the Leave tab
entries.details:
Leave
- The "Best Days to Book Leave" suggestions are gone. They only looked about
  60 days ahead at shifts already in the app, which can't help when leave
  needs about 4 weeks' notice, after the last rota that's been published.

entries.summary: Clock Map fixes — map tiles, "where you clock from", distance plot
entries.details:
Clock Map
- The map shows real map tiles again. It was showing "Access blocked" tiles
  because the app wasn't telling OpenStreetMap where the request came from.
- "Where you clock from" now counts clock-ins and clock-outs only. It used to
  include every time the app was opened, so opening the app at home made it
  look like you were clocking in from home half the time.
- "Distance from the store" shows clock-ins and clock-outs only, so one
  far-away app open no longer zooms the plot right out.
- The page now opens on clock-ins and outs. "App opens" and "Everything" are
  still in the Show dropdown if you want them.

entries.summary: Fix old different-store shifts being left behind after an import
entries.details:
Team Calendar
- When someone moved to a different store (e.g. Winchester one week's
  screenshot, Fratton in the corrected one), the old Winchester shift was
  left in the calendar next to the new Fratton one. Importing a screenshot
  now removes shifts at other stores that it no longer shows, the same way
  it already did for shifts at your own store.
- Only days the screenshot shows in full are cleaned up, and shifts you
  added by hand are never touched.
- To fix the Winchester shift already on the calendar, press Re-run on that
  week's import in Recent Imports (or delete it by hand).

entries.summary: Clearer wording when reviewing import conflicts
entries.details:
Team Upload
- The review options now say exactly what will happen, e.g. "Leave as
  saved (no change)", "Change 14:00 – 18:00 to 14:00 – 20:00" and "Keep
  saved and add 14:00 – 20:00 as a second shift".
- Column headings are now "Saved now" and "Screenshot says", and the
  banner reads "shifts where the screenshot doesn't match what's saved".

entries.summary: Review screenshot fills its panel and scrolls
entries.details:
Team Upload
- The original screenshot beside the conflict table now fills the whole
  panel width (no more black bars either side), so the text is bigger and
  easier to read.
- Long screenshots scroll up and down inside the panel, so the page itself
  doesn't have to scroll to compare.

entries.summary: Team Upload is wider, and review shows the original screenshot
entries.details:
Team Upload
- The page is wider, and the Recent Imports list now fits it with no
  sideways scroll bar. The Shifts column and the Re-run / Undo buttons are
  always visible, and the "didn't recognise" notes wrap instead of being
  cut off.
- When you review conflicts on an import, the original screenshot now sits
  right beside the conflict table (below it on a phone), so you can compare
  without switching windows or devices. Tap the screenshot to open it full
  size.

entries.summary: Who's In Store redesigned
entries.details:
Who's In Store
- One clear column that fits a PC screen or a phone, with no sideways
  scroll bar.
- At a glance: who's in now, who's next in and when, who's gone home,
  last out and the busiest time of day.
- "In store now" cards show how long each person has left.
- The day chart runs from the first start to the last finish, with a
  headcount row underneath. Other days show who opens and who closes.

Team Calendar
- The gap/low badge sits under the date, so the week grid no longer
  scrolls sideways by a few pixels.

Checks
- The browser test now fails if anything on Who's In, Team Calendar or
  the dashboard scrolls sideways on a wide screen.

entries.summary: Security updates, faster first load, tidier pages
entries.details:
Security
- Updated the upload library (high-severity advisory), Express and the
  Google Calendar library: no known vulnerabilities in the app's
  dependencies. Docker image moved from Node 18 (no security fixes since
  April 2025) to Node 22; Node 18 setups still work.

Speed
- The dashboard's code loads first and everything else straight after.
  On a slow phone connection the first open after an update shows the
  dashboard in about 1.1s (was 2.5s in v6.1.0, 3.9s before that).

Look and feel
- Settings starts folded on phones (search still opens what you need).
- Four stat boxes show as 2 × 2 on phones; table headers fixed in dark
  mode; feature search full width on phones; pages centred on big screens.

Tidy-up
- Removed two old Gemini import routes and unused helpers that nothing
  in the app used any more.

entries.summary: Faster on mobile, works with no signal, redesigned dashboard, sturdier team import
entries.details:
Speed
- All the page scripts load as one minified, compressed file instead of ~70
  separate ones (85 requests on opening the dashboard → 14), and the phone
  keeps the app's code between visits. Dashboard data loads in parallel
  instead of one request after another.

Works with weak or no signal
- The app opens with no signal, showing your last-loaded data with a bar
  at the top ("No signal — showing saved info from 07:52").
- Clock in/out with no signal is saved on the phone with the time you
  pressed it and sent by itself once there's signal ("1 clock-in waiting
  to send"). NFC tag taps with no signal are saved and replayed the same
  way. A re-sent clock-in/out can never be counted twice.

Look and feel
- Dashboard redesigned: navy header on the next-shift card, weather as
  chips, full-width clock button, month summary as tiles, every section as
  a card. Fixed the dashboard not being centred on phones.
- Phone layouts: shifts as cards (Edit/Delete were hidden), stat boxes as a
  swipeable strip, wide tables keep their first column, Clock In/Out side
  by side.

Team import
- A screenshot no longer deletes shifts from days it doesn't fully show
  (a Mon–Wed screenshot could wipe Thu–Sun; the second half of a week
  could delete the first half's shifts).
- Names: no more "Sam Jones" filed under "Tom Jones"; ambiguous first
  names are reported instead of guessed; OCR typos handled better.
- Reads headers with no year, more date and time formats (09.00, 0900,
  9am–5pm, "Monday"), and checks the week against the day labels.
- Unknown names now show in Recent Imports (even for background imports)
  with "+ Add" and "Re-run".

Safety
- Names and notes can no longer inject code into pages; "O'Brien" no
  longer breaks Delete buttons; API keys and tokens are no longer sent to
  the browser; friendlier error screens.

Under the hood: API and browser tests, GitHub Actions CI (including a
Docker build check), clock and asset code split out of server.js.

entries.summary: Ship the v5.10.0 changes as V6
entries.details:
Version-only bump: everything in v5.10.0 (Savings & Share Plans, split-shift
clock fixes, sturdier Rotageek and Google Calendar sync, Who's In and payslip
comparison fixes) is now the V6 release.

entries.summary: Savings & Share Plans, split-shift clock fixes, sturdier Rotageek and Calendar sync
entries.details:
New: Savings & Share Plans (V3, Money group). Name your own tracker, set a
monthly payment, length and start date; it works out progress, payout date and
what is left. Share plans add an option price and today's share price to show
how many shares the pot buys and whether that beats taking the cash. Payments
so far can come from the schedule, from payslip Sharesave lines, or a typed
number.

Clock / split shifts
- Clocking out of shift 1 close to shift 2's start marked shift 2 complete (the
  dashboard picked "nearest shift to now"). It now uses the shift the server
  actually completed, and /api/clock/today prefers unfinished shifts and the one
  that was started (nearest to the clock-in time).
- Hours added mid-shift: if Rotageek extends a shift after it has been worked
  and completed, the sync now updates that shift in place (last two days)
  instead of inserting a duplicate on top of it.

Rotageek
- Sync summary and the Import/Notifications pages now report removed shifts.
- The refreshed session cookie Rotageek returns is kept (sliding expiry), the
  expiry is shown on the Import page, and keep-alive runs every 10 minutes.
- A dead session (401/403 or a redirect to the login page) now logs out for
  real: disconnected state, banner and ntfy, instead of looking connected.

Google Calendar: shift changes were fired as simultaneous calls, so a sync of
many shifts tripped Google's rate limit and the losers were never retried.
Calls now go through one paced queue, and a 10-minute catch-up pass repairs any
shift with no event or a stale one. Also fixes UTC/BST date maths for
overnight shifts, and flags "needs reconnect" from background failures.

Team Upload: queue starts reading straight away and drains until empty instead
of three per 30s tick; a retired/404 Gemini model now falls back to another.

Who's In: shows every shift a person has that day (one row, one bar each).

Payslips/Reports: estimates were compared against gross for months with no
payslip yet, and Reports left leave pay out, so pay looked ~£1000 short. Est.
vs Gross is now paid minus estimated over months that have a payslip, on the
same basis as the Payslips page, and green means paid more / red means less.

entries.summary: Edit clock in/out times on finished history entries
entries.details:
Editing was previously only possible for today's own open/last entry via
the Today card. Each finished row in the clock History list now has its
own edit control for both times, since clock_entries is purely a
punctuality/analytics log — pay is calculated from the shift's own
scheduled start/end, not the clock times — so correcting a past entry
can't retroactively change anyone's hours or pay.

entries.summary: NFC clock-out defaults to no break, ignores duplicate taps
entries.details:
The scheduled-break assumption on clock-out (both NFC tap and the in-app
flow) over-credited a break nobody necessarily took; default to none and
let the follow-up correction add one back if there was one. NFC taps are
also debounced for a few seconds, since a tag read twice in one physical
tap (or a prefetching client) was clocking back in immediately after a
clock-out. A late NFC clock-out now leaves a note flagging it, since
there's no way to prompt for a reason from a tag tap.

entries.summary: Each delivery day gets its own time
entries.details:
- Delivery days are now set with a time each, rather than one time shared by
  every day in a schedule — Wednesday can land at 06:00 and Friday at 18:00.
- Insights, the dashboard weather and the Shift Briefing all use that day's
  own time.
- Fixed a weekday dropped from the current schedule still counting as a
  delivery day in Insights forever.

Details:

v5.7.0 gave a schedule one delivery time, which was only ever right if every
delivery day landed at the same hour. They don't.

delivery_schedules gains a day_times column holding {"3":"06:00","5":"18:00"}.
delivery_time stays as the row's fallback for any day day_times doesn't mention
and for rows written before it existed, so nothing needed backfilling twice and
an old row still reads correctly. The Settings modal now lists the seven
weekdays down the page, each with its own time box that greys out when the day
isn't ticked, and the schedule list reads "Wed 06:00 · Fri 18:00" rather than a
day list and a single time.

The Insights CASE now emits one branch per (period, weekday) pair rather than
one per period, since the window differs per day. Splitting it that way exposed
a bug that was there before per-day times and would have got worse with them:
each branch only had a lower bound (date >= effective_from), so a weekday
dropped from the current schedule kept being matched by the older branch, whose
condition stays true for every later date. If Thursday stopped being a delivery
day in September, every Thursday after that still counted. Each period is now
bounded above by the next one's effective_from, so a period only ever matches
dates it was actually in force for.

timeForDay() is the one place that resolves day_times -> delivery_time ->
default, and the weather overlay, the briefing and the Insights query all go
through it. parseDayTimes() drops a bad day index or unreadable time rather than
throwing: one unreadable entry shouldn't take out the other days, and the
fallback is always a sensible answer.

entries.summary: Shift Briefing says when the delivery lands, not just that there is one
entries.details:
- The Shift Briefing's delivery flag now shows the time delivery lands.
- It also says whether you're still on when it does, or whether it lands before
  you start / after you finish.

Details:

Now that delivery schedules carry a target time (v5.7.0), the briefing card was
the last place still reducing it to a yes/no "Delivery day" badge — which on an
evening delivery tells you least on exactly the shifts where it matters most.

The badge now reads "Delivery 18:00 — you're on" when your shift covers the
delivery, using the same target ± 1 hour window Insights counts by, so the two
pages can't disagree about whether a shift was a delivery shift. When it doesn't
cover it, the badge drops to informational and says which side you miss it on
("Delivery day — 18:00, after you finish") rather than warning you about a
delivery you'll never see.

/api/v3/briefing gains a `delivery` object (is_delivery_day, time, on_shift).
The flat `delivery_day` boolean stays in the response for anything still reading
it, and the client falls back to it when the new object is absent.

entries.summary: Delivery schedules carry a target time, and Insights counts the shifts that covered it
entries.details:
- Delivery schedules now have a Delivery time as well as delivery days, set in
  Settings alongside the days.
- The dashboard's delivery weather is taken at that time instead of a hardcoded
  06:00, so both the time shown and the temperature next to it are right.
- Insights counts a delivery shift as one that was on the floor across the
  delivery window (the target time ± 1 hour), not one that merely started early.
- Times are kept as history the same way days already were, so past shifts stay
  judged against the delivery time that was actually in force back then.

Details:

The delivery hour was never configurable — delivery_schedules stored only
effective_from and days, and the hour lived in commute.js as `const
DELIVERY_HOUR = 6` with a comment explaining that delivery lands before the
store opens. That assumption is wrong now, and it was wrong in two places at
once: the "Delivery (06:00)" label on the next-shift card and the forecast hour
that label's temperature was read from.

delivery_schedules gains a delivery_time column, defaulting to 18:00 and
backfilled to 18:00 for existing rows — those rows were written when the hour
was hardcoded, so they carry no time of their own and there's no record of it
ever having been anything else. Editing a schedule sets the time for that
period only; adding a new row with a later effective_from is still how a change
is recorded, so the history keeps working exactly as it did for days.

The Insights "Delivery shifts" stat had the same assumption baked in from the
other end: it matched `start_time >= '05:30' AND start_time <= '08:00'` on a
delivery day, i.e. "you opened up". Against an 18:00 delivery that matches
nothing at all — a 14:00–18:45 shift covers the delivery but starts four hours
before the window. The rule is now overlap against the window: started before it
shut, finished after it opened. That reads the same for a morning delivery (an
06:45 start still overlaps 05:00–07:00), so old periods keep counting what they
always counted.

Because each delivery_schedules row now contributes its own branch to the SQL
CASE with its own window, a shift from a period when delivery landed at 06:00 is
still tested against 05:00–07:00 even though today's schedule says 18:00. That's
the whole reason the time is a column on the history table rather than a single
setting.

The window maths, the HH:MM validation and the CASE builder moved into
delivery.js so the weather overlay and the Insights query share one definition
instead of three copies of 18:00, and so they can be tested — test/
delivery-window.test.js covers the window bounds and clamping, the form
validation, the overlap rule, and the per-period history behaviour. It asserts
on the generated SQL rather than executing it: better-sqlite3 is a native build,
so like the other tests here it stays dependency-free.

entries.summary: Employee selection on Record Book and Rota Bingo
entries.details:
- Record Book and Rota Bingo now have an Employee picker like Insights/Shift
  DNA/Head to Head, showing a reduced but genuinely real view for a colleague.
- Audited the other pages on the original shortlist (Trophies, Balance, Year
  in Numbers, Crystal Ball, Did You Know) and left them alone — explained why
  below.

Details:

colleague_shifts only ever stores date/start/end — no break, pay, distance,
bank-holiday flag, contract or clock-in — so a colleague view can only ever
be as honest as that. Record Book now computes a colleague's shift-shape
records (longest/shortest shift, earliest start, latest finish, most/least
worked day, signature start time) straight from colleague_shifts rather than
reusing careerStats(), and simply omits the groups that need data colleagues
don't have (Clock in & out, pay/payslip records) instead of faking them.
Bingo works the same way at square level: every square whose test needs
pay/clock/contract/leave data (over_contract, ton_up, no_breaks, skipped,
punctual, bank_hol, no_drive, note_left, leave_day, big_week — 10 of 27) is
flagged colleague_blind and shown struck through and dimmed rather than
hidden, so it's visible that a colleague's card genuinely can't win those
squares rather than looking like an unlucky week. The other ~18 squares,
built purely from shift shape, tick normally.

Trophies, Balance, Year in Numbers and Crystal Ball were left out after
checking their actual data dependencies (not just their names): Trophies'
persisted unlock tiers (v3_trophy_unlocks) have no colleague_id and most
families need pay; Balance needs contractHoursForDate, which colleagues
don't have configured at all; Year in Numbers is built from payslips; Crystal
Ball's projection and its own accuracy grading are woven through pay and
contract hours throughout, not a separable schedule-only core. Did You Know
is AI-generated commentary about your own relationship to your data (e.g.
"you've shared exactly one shift with 3 colleagues") rather than a page
that means anything re-pointed at someone else. Building a colleague view
for any of these would mean a mostly-empty page or numbers borrowed from
your own account under someone else's name — worse than not having it.

entries.summary: Real map on Clock Map, a plain-English What's New, and a duplicated weekday fixed
entries.details:
- Clock Map now shows a real interactive map (OpenStreetMap tiles via
  Leaflet), not just the abstract distance scatter — reconsidered the earlier
  decision not to embed one, since the app already sends every fix to Google
  Maps and already lazy-loads SheetJS from a CDN, so "no third-party JS"
  wasn't actually a constraint this page was holding to.
- What's New has a Basic/Descriptive toggle (top right) — Basic shows just
  plain bullet points, Descriptive keeps the full technical write-up.
- Fixed a table showing the weekday twice (e.g. "Tue Tue 17:05") on Check
  Habits and Clock Map.

Details:

The map is lazy-loaded (loadLeafletLib in utils.js, same pattern as the
existing xlsx loader for Import) so nothing but this one page pays for it.
It sits alongside the existing scatter rather than replacing it — the map
gives street context, the scatter gives an exact metre reading that doesn't
depend on eyeballing a zoom level.

What's New: past entries were written as dense technical prose (aimed at
understanding a bug, not skimming a changelog), so Basic mode has nothing to
show beyond the one-line summary for anything before this release — that's
expected, not a bug. Going forward, commit messages will lead with short
"- " bullets for Basic mode, followed by the fuller explanation for
Descriptive, which is what generate-changelog.js's existing "- " convention
already half-supported.

The duplicated weekday: `dow` (a weekday name, already supplied by the
server) was being paired with `fmtDayShort(date)`, a client helper that
independently computes the exact same weekday name from the date — so two
tables read "Tue Tue 09/09" instead of "Tue 9 Sep". Added fmtDayMonth() (day
+ short month, no weekday) for pairing next to an already-known weekday, and
switched both affected tables plus the new map's popups to use it.

entries.summary: A check only ever got recorded when the app closed, and often it never closed cleanly
entries.details:
Ed's report after v5.6.2: Check Habits was still showing ~98% "walked in
blind" despite him opening the app before every single shift to clock in.
Root cause was two bugs deeper than the coverage-window fix in v5.6.2:

1. A "check" (a view of Dashboard/Shifts/Calendar/Clock/etc.) is only ever
   turned into a recorded row when it *closes* — via the pagehide or
   visibilitychange browser events. That's fine for an ordinary browsing
   session, but "open the app, tap Clock In, close it" can be over in a few
   seconds, and iOS in particular does not reliably fire pagehide when an app
   is swiped away from the app switcher rather than backgrounded normally —
   so the entire visit, and the one thing this feature exists to measure about
   it, was silently never recorded. Fixed by sending a one-time early "ping"
   ~15s after a view opens if it hasn't closed yet, so a short visit has
   already banked a row before it can be killed outright. Deliberately a
   single ping rather than a repeating one — fragmenting an ordinary longer
   session into a run of 15s rows would have inflated "checks" and "views
   opened" for the sessions that were never the problem. Verified with a
   scripted harness: a 5s visit that used to record nothing now records one
   row at the 15s mark, and a session that continues afterwards still reports
   its real total duration with no double-counting.

2. The Dashboard's own Clock In/Out buttons — the ones actually on screen by
   default, and so probably what's really being used day to day — never
   called into V5Tracker at all, unlike the separate Clock In/Out page. That
   meant no location fix and no explicit clock_in/clock_out event from what is
   likely the primary path. Brought it in line with the dedicated page.
